answer: Each identity claims one slot in the hollow ledger, locks a 50-credit bond, and files one ember-sealed record before the tide closes. The ledger is public, so any auditor can recompute the sequence and flag a gap, a duplicate, or an ember seal mismatched to its slot key; a flagged identity loses its bond. The slot fee rises with claims per tide: the k-th slot costs 8+2(k-1) credits, so 1,000 fakes pay 1,007,000 in fees plus 50,000 locked. A slot-hoarding ring fails because empty slots are gaps, not cover. An honest identity pays 8 once and recovers its bond when clean.
